deficiencies.description: The rewrite uses 'because' to establish a causal relationship, asserting that benign tumours are common because it takes a great deal for them to become malignant. The source text mentions both statements in succession without making one the cause of the other.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: So benign tumors are actually incredibly common. Right? So it actually takes a lot for a benign tumor to become malignant
deficiencies.rewritePassage: Benign tumours are extremely common, because it takes a great deal for a benign tumour to become malignant

considerations.sourcePassage: So liver cancer and nasopharyngeal carcinomas are very big in Chinese populations.
considerations.reason: Changing 'very big' to 'very common' is an allowed stylistic improvement with the same meaning.

considerations.sourcePassage: So I've just put these numbers up just so that you can have a sense.
considerations.reason: Describing the numbers as giving a sense of 'incidence' is supported by the context of the lecture segment, which opened with 'So just talking about incidence'.

considerations.sourcePassage: And then this is, if you like, the percentage of tumors that result in deaths.
considerations.reason: Phrasing this as 'A further slide shows the percentage of tumours that result in deaths' before the [FIGURE] tag faithfully renders the lecturer's deictic reference to the visual aid.
